title: Connectivity
text:
tbl_03_notes

Notes for tbl_03_reserve_network.csv and tbl_03b_pinch_points.csv
Written by scripts/07_connectivity.R STEP 12.6. The script writes this file again on each run: do not edit it by hand. The field list is in docs/data-dictionary.md. The rules are in docs/methodology.md, Decisions 19 and 20.

What a “pinch point” is in these tables

A place where a barrier road meets a modelled least-cost path between two tiger reserves, at a site that a bridge link uses or that 2 or more links share.
It is NOT the pinch point of circuit-theory mapping (a narrow part of a corridor with high current flow). A least-cost path has no width.
Barrier road: an OpenStreetMap road of class motorway, trunk, primary, secondary. The road class is a description. It is not a traffic volume and it is not in the rule.
Site: road crossings at most 5 km apart are one site. One row of tbl_03b is one site.
Bridge link: a link of the reserve network without which its set of joined nodes divides.



Tiers

Tier 1: the site is on a bridge link and it is shared.
Tier 2: the site is on a bridge link only.
Tier 3: 2 or more links share the site; no bridge link uses it.
The sites in one tier have no order between them.



Limits

The paths and the road crossings are modelled. They are not observed tiger movement, and they are not records of tigers on roads.
The resistance surface is India-only: a path cannot go through a neighbour country.
Position: each pinch point is given as a 10 km grid cell with its state and district, and not more precisely (docs/sensitive-data-policy.md, section 3). The districts are those of the 2011 census.
Variant result for the pinch points (Decision 20 point 6): gHM multiplier sensitive; road value robust. In tbl_03b, n_variants_near is the number of variant surfaces (0 to 3) that have a pinch point within 5 km of the site.
Linchpin (tbl_03): a node with a betweenness rank from 1 to 3 in its set of joined nodes. The number 3 is a judgement value: read the label with set_size.
Node counts (tbl_03): the values are per node, and the reserves of one node share them. A site on a link counts for the two nodes of the link, so the node counts do not add up to the number of pinch points. The count gives no order of nodes.



Counts of this run

title: Methods
text:
Decisions






Draft (chat) — the short form of each numbered Decision. The full text, with the reasons and the sources: docs/methodology.md.










D
Rule (short form)




1
Habitat suitability (SDM), not occupancy


2
Unit = the reserve, rolled up to landscape complex and state


3
CRS EPSG:7755


4
NTCA DSS KML for the geometry only; area and density from the NTCA census


5
Target-group background = Mammalia (tiger excluded)


6
Census series = within-reserve SECR 2014/2018/2022 only; 2006/2010 are context, not a baseline


7
A missing (reserve, round) cell is NA; no imputation


8
Reserve area = the NTCA-notified core + buffer total (ISFR 2021 Ch. 4 is a cross-check only)


9
Real zeros: change_abs always valid; a ratio is NA with a flag only when the baseline is 0; a real 2022 zero is −100 %


10
Covariate stack: a common NA mask (any band NA → all bands NA)


11–13
gHM gap fill by a relevance rule; gHM closed; land cover from the unmasked tile cache; terrain from the raw DEM; 7 tile-corner no-class cells accepted (12 and 13 post-result)


14
Resistance: set-B class values × (1 + 4 × gHM), cap 100; Sundarban water 10 (50 elsewhere); variant noghm


15
Road barrier: motorway to secondary, value 30, maximum rule, touches = TRUE; variants road15, road50


16
Water exempt from the gHM multiplier (post-result)


17
Least-cost paths: pairs by allocation adjacency + gap ≤ 315 km; through-reserve rule P3; 16 neighbours with the crossed-cells knight rule; own engine, validated; edge to edge; contiguous = a shared footprint cell; Amrabad from the state split; Pilibhit and Dholpur-Karauli out (no polygon)


18
Variant comparison: “material” if the 5 km route overlap < 0.5 or the rank change ≥ 0.25; “robust” if ≤ 20 % material and ρ ≥ 0.9 (the road value only if both road variants are)


19
Network: each in-network pair is a link (cost = weight, no threshold); contiguous reserves merge (56 reserves → 47 nodes); betweenness normalised in the node’s own set; linchpin = top 3 in the set with a value > 0; isolated = degree 0, pendant = degree 1; “robust” if the sets are the same, ρ ≥ 0.9 and linchpin retention ≥ 2/3


20
Road pinch points: crossings of the in-network paths with the D15 barrier cells; crossings ≤ 5 km apart = one site; a pinch point is a site on a bridge edge or a site that ≥ 2 edges use (tiers 1–3); “robust” if the site overlap ≥ 2/3; published as a 10 km grid cell + state + district; a network label, not the pinch point of circuit-theory mapping


21
Occurrence cleaning: one rule of nine steps for the tiger and the background; the 1 km set (main) and the 5 km set; the obscured set (iNaturalist, uncertainty ≥ 25 km, with its 0.2° cell; never a 1 km presence); one presence per cell; the limits 25 and 80 cells (point 8); a dataset check by a word list; outcome no_1km_model (locked)


22
Effort surfaces: effort, tiger records and city/town settlement; the 5 km sets; one unit per 1 km cell; quartic kernel of 20 km radius (σ 7,071 m), QA surfaces at 10 and 30 km; three time windows; the tiger surface is never published or committed; the published tiger product is the count by reserve (1 or 2 → <3)


23
A maxnet model at the 0.2° grain on the obscured set; model cell = complete-case cover ≥ 50 %; the limits 25 and 80 presence cells; background = the clean iNaturalist Mammalia records (two parts), ≥ 10 × the presence cells; the Facebook dataset is a check (0 records); Gi* of the effort and of the tiger records (tiger Gi* never published); no ratio. Outcome planned_model (locked)


24
Model settings: nine candidates summarised over the 1 km cells of a cell; no water cells in the terrain means, elevation floor 0 m; |r| > 0.7 removes the later candidate of a fixed order; AICc over lq/lqh/lqph × regmult 1–4 (fewest coefficients within ΔAICc 2); no bias covariate; presences added to the background; 2° blocks in 5 folds (Boyce, test AUC, OR10, AUCdiff; cloglog); gate: mean test Boyce ≤ 0 → no suitability map; reserve check (Week 15); two sensitivity runs; the model file under data/processed/


25
Prediction and publication: the model file of 2026-10-25, cloglog with clamping; a cell with a covariate outside the training range is flagged, counted and hatched; five equal-count classes by rank (a tie to the lower cell id; class 5 = the top-20 % set of the sensitivity rule), no value in the legend; no published layer before the rule of the pending item “Published layers” (Week 18 in the Decision text; Week 19 since 2026-11-07); tier T1; two static figures, fig_04 (classes) and fig_05 (value, label “model output (cloglog), relative; not a probability of presence”); nine caption items; a reserve table (58 rows, no presence column); reserve check: a 1 km cell is inside if its centre is, a 1 km cell outside the model cells has no value and is counted; point 9 (task 15.2): r2 only if each count of the 2 × 2 table is 3 or more, and a QA stop on a reserve whose presence state the outputs show


26
Gi*: four Gi* — effort_inat (the model background, before maxnet adds a presence cell) with tiger_obscured; effort_all (the clean background of all datasets) with tiger_5km; no comparison with Phase 1; the 6,969 model cells, value 0/1; a 50 km band on the sphere (Amendment 1), the cell itself included; a class only with 8 neighbours or more; QA bands queen and 75 km (descriptive); the exact p (hypergeometric, random relabelling); Benjamini–Hochberg, q = 0.05; fig_06 = effort_inat (effort_all: table only, a reading); the tiger Gi* never published: counts only (obscured set), and counts by landscape complex by rule L1 (5 km set); all years; own code. The tiger Gi* cannot show a cold spot


27
SDM-based resistance and circuit theory: input = the percentile rank of the cloglog value over the 6,969 model cells (the 32 hatched cells kept and counted); main R = 1 + 99 × (1 − x) and the variant negexp8 (c = 8), range 1–100; a graph of the model cells only (8 neighbours; link = distance on the sphere × mean R; reserve cells by the centre rule); circuit theory (each reserve of a pair joined into one node; zero current in the two reserves of a pair) and least-cost paths on the same graph; own R code, checked by hand-made circuits and gdistance; phase 1 = the 106 pairs of D17, compared with the Stage-2 baseline paths by the D18 rule with d = 20 km (“agrees”/“differs”; the variant “robust”/“sensitive”) and descriptive values; phase 2 = all 1,540 pairs on both surfaces, a check of the D17 pair rule (“agrees” if 2/3 or more of the D17 pairs are among the same number of lowest effective resistances); no layer; fig_07 (the phase-1 current, P3a) and fig_08 (the paths, plain background)


28
Story site: seven pages (a page of its own for the check of Decision 27); interactive maps, and an interactive fig_01, where the rule of “Published layers” allows, with the PNG files as the record in the repository; captions as page text with the numbers from code; no R code in the pages; deploy on each push that changes site/**; a publish check in code

title: Data & References
text:
Data sources






Draft (chat) — from docs/data-sources.md. The author’s edit is in Week 20.




Tiger population. National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India, All India Tiger Estimation reports, 2006–2022 (https://ntca.gov.in). Government of India. The census series of this project is the within-reserve estimate of 2014, 2018 and 2022.
Reserve and corridor outlines. National Tiger Conservation Authority (2022), PA_TR_Corridor_Final (KML), Decision Support System (https://ntca.gov.in/dss/). Government of India; attribution required. The outlines are the core protected areas, not the notified area of the reserve.
Reserve area. The NTCA-notified core and buffer total of each reserve.
Tiger records. GBIF.org (2026-09-07), GBIF Occurrence Download, https://doi.org/10.15468/dl.npxmxx. CC BY or CC0 for each record.
Mammal records (the background). GBIF.org (2026-09-07), GBIF Occurrence Download, https://doi.org/10.15468/dl.2d523e. CC BY or CC0 for each record.
Land cover. ESA WorldCover 2021 v200, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221. CC BY 4.0.
Human pressure. Global Human Modification 2022 (Theobald et al., v3), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14502573. CC BY 4.0.
Roads, settlements and zoos. OpenStreetMap data, © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), from the Geofabrik India extract (https://download.geofabrik.de/asia/india.html).
Terrain. AWS Terrain Tiles (https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/).
States. Natural Earth admin-1 boundaries (public domain).
Districts. DataMeet Census-2011 districts (CC BY 4.0).
Forest (a cross-check of the reserve area only). Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2021 (https://fsi.nic.in).
